A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ReCOT, with matching architecture, equations, experiments, and supplementary material. Their readable text, tables, and rendered figures support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original ReCOT benchmark results, component and hyperparameter ablations, runtime measurements, and qualitative analyses in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: V2 retains original ReCOT experiments and additionally reports few-shot evaluation and a SAM-versus-EdgeSAM supervision ablation.

M1.justification: The recurrent token updates, box prediction, RFEM, SAM distillation, and training losses remain unchanged. V2 adds implementation explanations and changes evaluation configurations; EdgeSAM appears as an ablation rather than a replacement in the proposed method.

E1.justification: V2 adds CVOGL-few-shot evaluation on four new object categories: lake, parking, slide, and port. This extends coverage to novel-category, limited-data adaptation. The original ground-to-satellite and drone-to-satellite dataset remains; its shortened name, CVOGL, does not denote another new dataset.

E2.justification: Main Table 4 adds TROGeo, GeoFormer, and AttenGeo, while removing OCGNet from the standard-benchmark comparison. The supplementary backbone comparison also replaces OCGNet with newer comparators. OCGNet remains evaluated in the new few-shot comparison, so it is not removed throughout the paper. HALO is cited but has no reported comparison row.

E3.justification: The stated learning rate changes from 0.0025 to 0.000025, and the 300-epoch specification is replaced by training to convergence. Table 1 changes from test-set accuracy analysis to validation-set average IoU, Acc@0.50, and runtime analysis. V2 selects m=5 for both tasks, replacing v1's task-specific and inconsistent drone-step recommendations. Few-shot evaluation introduces pretrained-checkpoint fine-tuning with 28 training and 24 test samples. These are reported protocol changes; the PDFs do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds a SAM-versus-EdgeSAM ablation testing sensitivity to supervision quality and recurrent-step experiments under few-shot adaptation. The existing step-count analysis is revised to examine validation performance and runtime. Component, RFEM, token-count, loss-weight, and backbone analyses remain, as do the existing attention visualizations and failure cases.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Both present point estimates without statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The headline drone Acc@0.25/Acc@0.50 changes from 78.21/72.35 to 77.60/72.05 under the revised step setting; the latter values already appeared at m=5 in v1. Reported headline speed changes from 25.7 to 24.3 FPS. V2 adds newer-baseline, validation-step, EdgeSAM, and few-shot results, including 50.00/33.33 for few-shot ReCOT at m=6. Most comparative validation entries are removed. These are revised and additional results, not established same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The method equations and loss definitions are retained. Acc@t and IoU definitions move from the supplement into the main text without mathematical changes. New discussion of residual corrections and convergence is qualitative; no new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same three central contributions: token-driven recurrent localization, SAM distillation without additional inference cost, and hierarchical RFEM. The central claims of state-of-the-art accuracy, fewer parameters, and competitive speed also remain. V2 expands supporting evidence and the recurrence rationale without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: New discussion attributes attainable accuracy primarily to recurrence and treats complementary modules as improving the starting point. V2 adds explanations of saturation, tolerance to imperfect SAM masks, and differences from architectural scaling. V1's discussion of occlusion- and clutter-limited ground-view gains is removed. The ambiguous-point-prompt limitation remains, while adaptive stopping becomes an additional future direction.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-access link, identifies DETR-style positional embedding, specifies single-RTX-4090 timing and the task used for headline FPS, and documents few-shot checkpoint initialization. It revises the stated learning rate while dropping the explicit PyTorch and 300-epoch disclosures. These are documentation and access-information changes; repository availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: V2 expands positioning against recent CVOGL work, including TROGeo, GeoFormer, AttenGeo, and HALO. A new supplementary discussion distinguishes shared recurrent updates from GeoFormer's independently parameterized stacked decoder and discusses a DETR-like interpretation. Additional citations support step selection, token scaling, and EdgeSAM; the PyTorch reference is removed.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most method prose are retained. V2 revises portions of the motivation, related work, and experimental narrative, adds discussion subsections, moves metric definitions into the main text, and updates terminology, subsection numbering, authors, and affiliations.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document from two columns to one and extensively rearranges displays. Main Table 4 removes validation columns and incorporates parameter/runtime columns from the former efficiency table. Few-shot and teacher-ablation tables are added, and Figures 1 and 4 are redrawn with revised annotations. Existing qualitative and failure-case figures are largely retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: V2's validation-based step selection resolves v1's inconsistent drone-step recommendations and improves the reported evaluation procedure. Few-shot experiments, newer baselines, and the teacher ablation strengthen empirical support. These gains are tempered by removing OCGNet from the standard-benchmark comparison and dropping the explicit training budget. The resulting quality improvement is supported but limited.
